definition: Hegemony means the controlling dominance of one power over the rest.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word hegemony. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know hegemony should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Nobody voted for English's hegemony over the sciences; laboratories in forty countries simply stopped publishing in anything else.
Leverage is far short of hegemony — strength for one negotiation, a good hand in a single game, spent when the deal closes; hegemony is a standing position the whole field steers by.
Empire goes further than hegemony — the hegemon's rivals keep their own flags and follow its lead; an empire hauls the flags down and rules directly.

Dominance is the plain word for being on top, and it can be won one contest at a time — a team can dominate a season and be gone the next. Hegemony adds the standing arrangement: the others steer by the leader's lead and reshape their own plans around it.

Supremacy is the title for holding top rank — a claim about position, the name engraved on the trophy. Hegemony is the working arrangement underneath: one power setting terms that its supposed equals follow. Supremacy can be asserted in a slogan; hegemony shows up in everyone else's behavior.

Greek hegemon, the leader, produced hegemony and its adjective hegemonic — and then stopped. No everyday English word shares the root, so anchor the meaning to the picture instead: one flag out front, and the rest of the fleet steering by it.

By 1900 the Blue Star line enjoyed a hegemony over the northern trade that no court had granted and no treaty named.
Its fleet had not won a race in years, and smaller companies still beat it on price along a dozen routes.
What mattered was quieter: rival captains set their sailing dates around its timetable, and insurers wrote their rates from its charts.
Ports deepened their harbors to fit its hulls before anyone thought to ask, and shipbuilders drew their new designs to match its docks.
The line issued no orders and needed none; the entire coast simply organized itself around the company's lead.
